affected_docs.why: Lines 111-113 state that day-to-day details of managing several personas, such as a settings screen for editing or removing one, are not yet covered by what ships today; a Personas page ships in all three clients and edits, removes, previews and re-grants. Lines 46-71 describe only the first-run interview and open at line 48 with 'The first time you open Hearth', so the page never states how a reader makes a persona after first run has ended. Three further claims on the page are contradicted by the same source tree: lines 83-86 (the engine reads the manifest off disk when it loads or switches), lines 95-96 (the designed clip is a permanent reference), and lines 96-100 (a pending voice design is picked up the first time the voice service is available).

Line 75 lists create_persona in a `projects` domain and lines 91-102 argue that the `projects` domain is granted to nobody, which states that create_persona cannot be reached in ordinary conversation. tools.yaml:1091 puts create_persona in the `personas` domain, no tool in tools.yaml carries a `projects` domain, and sulivan.json:72 grants `personas`. If T5 states on Personas that a reader can ask their persona to make another, this page states the opposite. Lines 92-93 also misreport Sulivan's grants, and line 51 misreports the catalog size.

sections: ## How a persona gets a voice
affected_docs.why: Lines 38-43 carry the same pending-voice claim as personas.md lines 96-100: 'The design is recorded and completed the next time the voice engine can run it.' Nothing in the tree reads the pending_design flag, so if the sentence on Personas is corrected this one must be corrected with it or the two concept pages disagree. Line 32 also states the clip becomes 'the persona's permanent reference', the same overreach as personas.md line 95.

Lines 287-292 state as an unsolved problem that 'Adding a persona needs cache invalidation, not a process exit'. creation.py lines 9-11 record that a new persona needs no invalidation, because discovery re-reads the directory and load() caches only names it has seen. If Personas states that making a second persona takes effect without restarting the house, this passage contradicts it. Note the overlap: T3 already owns this page for the install root and the 8 GB example, and this defect is in a different section.

claims.claim: create_persona is the only tool in the personas domain, so the grant enables creating a persona and nothing else.
claims.evidence: grep of `^    domain:` across backend/harness/valar/tools/tools.yaml returns one occurrence of `personas`, at line 1091, against 48 `- name:` entries and 13 distinct domains.

claims.claim: The grant reached the template on the current branch, and it changed only the template.
claims.evidence: git show 4ca4807 (fix(personas): a persona you made can make another persona, 2026-09-03) touches one file, backend/harness/valar/data/persona_template.json, adding "personas" to tool_grants.domains and extending the comment. No other file is in the diff.

claims.claim: The older account, in which the only route to a second persona was switching back to Sulivan, is superseded and must not be written.
claims.evidence: Superseded by backend/harness/valar/data/persona_template.json line 33 and the comment at line 32, which names that route and states nothing intended it. claims.claim: create_persona has no first-run gate: it is available in ordinary conversation to any persona whose grants include the personas domain.
claims.evidence: backend/harness/valar/gateway/voice_loop.py lines 1516-1533 return first_run.INTERVIEW_GRANTS while first run is active, first_run.BRAIN_GRANTS during the second-brain beat, and otherwise the persona's own tool_grants from its manifest. Lines 1628-1639 build the turn's registry from those grants. Nothing in backend/harness/valar/tools/handlers/creation.py tests for first run.

claims.claim: First run expires permanently the moment the first persona is written, so the guided interview cannot be the route to a second persona.
claims.evidence: backend/harness/valar/gateway/first_run.py lines 253-268 (_all_personas_shipped) return False as soon as one non-internal persona lacks "shipped": true, and lines 271-287 (active) are that check. The module docstring at lines 4-7 states it directly: 'The moment create_persona writes a new resident, the next turn's detection fails and everything here expires on its own.'

claims.claim: The reader triggers creation by asking the persona they already have; the persona composes the six fields from the conversation and calls create_persona once.
claims.evidence: backend/harness/valar/tools/tools.yaml lines 1084-1089 are the tool description the persona reads: 'Create a new persona from what the conversation taught you. Call this ONCE, only when you could describe this person to someone else: their purpose, their temperament, how they should sound, their colour. You write the system prompt IN THEIR VOICE, not yours.' Lines 1093-1127 are the parameters; the required set is name, description, system_prompt, temperament, colour, with voice_design optional.

claims.claim: Creating a persona outside first run differs from the first-run interview: there is no structured schema, no scripted opening, and no interview direction.

An ordinary turn takes the tool-loop path at voice_loop.py lines 1628-1639.

gaps: No page in the corpus documents the Personas page itself. desktop-client/src/components/personas/PersonasView.tsx line 28 names wiki/clients/persona-page.md as its design of record and that file does not exist; find wiki -name '*persona*' returns only features/personas.md, features/persona-face.md and three raw/ specs. wiki/features/persona-face.md line 117 refers to 'Personas > Animations' as though the page were described somewhere, and it is not.
No page states how a reader makes a persona after first run has ended. That is the gap T5 exists to close.
No page states that a persona made before commit 4ca4807 cannot make another, or names the two routes that work for such a reader.
No page states that removing a persona is behind developer mode, or that removal renames rather than deletes.
No page states that an edit on the Personas page restarts the house while making a persona does not.
No canonical or primary source outside the repository bears on any claim here. Hearth reaches no external service, so the source tree is the only authority and no external reference was sought.
open_questions: Does T5 own the corrections on wiki/backend/tool-catalog.md, wiki/features/voice.md and wiki/first-run.md, or do those need their own tracker rows? The tracker states at line 220 that task targets do not overlap, and T3 already owns wiki/first-run.md for a different defect in a different section. Each of the three contradicts what T5 will state on Personas, so none can simply be left.

Should Personas state that a persona made before this change cannot make another, or is that a release-note concern rather than a concept-page concern? The fact is verified either way (persona_template.json is expanded once at creation and nothing migrates an existing manifest), and the reader it affects is anyone whose house predates 2026-09-03.

Should Personas name the two developer-mode switches that gate Remove, or say only that removal is behind developer mode? Naming both is accurate (Settings > Developer > Developer mode, then the switch that appears on the Personas page itself) and may be more procedure than a concept page should carry under wiki/page-types.md lines 153-154.
